title: A colony that can breed digs a crater and halves the stand
question: Is a bed that ends up looking like the right-hand picture the dynamic you want the lab to have, or has the colony gone too far?
context_md:
Ants have never reproduced in this engine. They do now — same bed, same 24,000 frames, same shipped ant, and the only difference between the two pictures is **whether there was food lying on the ground for them to find**.

What I am unsure of is the *right-hand* picture, not the mechanism. A breeding colony strips the herb bed from 177 plants to 37 and excavates the pit in the middle. That may be exactly the grazer-versus-crop pressure the lab wants, or it may be a colony that eats its world and then dies with it.

Already measured, so please ignore: the ants do reproduce (generation 13), the food economy adds up, and nothing in the outdoor game changes visibly.

**The still cannot show the ants** — your own note that ants read by their motion holds here, and the dark specks in the pit are them. Judge the *bed*, not the animals.
